Operator:  
Good morning, and welcome to the Global Consumer Brands Inc., or GCB, Q3 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. During the Q&A session, please press star then one on your telephone keypad if you would like to ask a question. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.  

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations.  

Alex Rivera:  
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss GCB's Q3 results. With me on the call are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Marketing Officer; and David Ortiz, Chief Supply Chain Officer; and other members of our leadership team.  

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking and are based on our current expectations and beliefs. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.  

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.  

Sarah Thompson:  
Thank you, Alex. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. GCB delivered a solid Q3, demonstrating the resilience of our brands and the strength of our team. We are navigating a dynamic environment and remain focused on executing our strategic priorities.  

Our discussion today will cover our overall financial performance including organic sales growth and its decomposition, new product launches and innovation pipeline update, geographic performance across developed and emerging markets, promotional strategy and effectiveness, gross margin performance, and outlook for the remainder of the year.  

I will now turn the call over to Michael Chen to provide more detail on our financial results.  

Michael Chen:  
Thank you, Sarah. As Sarah mentioned, we delivered a solid quarter. Net sales were $4.5 billion, representing a 6.1% increase compared to the prior year on a reported basis and 5.8% organic growth on a constant currency basis. Gross margin was 42.5%, up 230 basis points year-over-year, driven by pricing discipline, productivity gains, and supply chain efficiencies that more than offset input cost inflation and logistics pressures. Operating income was $800 million, up 12% year-over-year. Diluted earnings per share were $1.42, reflecting 11% growth. We continue to manage our costs effectively and invest in our long-term growth initiatives.  

Let me start by diving deeper into our organic sales growth for the quarter. We're thrilled with the 5.8% year-over-year organic sales growth, which excludes the impact of a modest FX headwind from a stronger dollar and the prior year's divestiture of a non-core European pet food unit. On a two-year stacked basis, this puts us at around 10%, outpacing the CPG industry average of about 6% per NielsenIQ data. This marks our sixth straight quarter of positive momentum, ahead of peers like Procter & Gamble and Unilever.  

Volume grew a healthy 2.0%, supported by share gains in high-velocity categories like snacks and beverages, while price/mix added a robust 3.8%. Premiumization continues to be key, with higher average selling prices from innovations such as our reformulated zero-sugar beverages and plant-based dairy alternatives.  

In beverages, which make up 42% of sales, we saw 6.5% organic growth, with volume up 2.3% from adding thousands of SKUs in club channels like Costco and distribution gains in hydration products akin to the explosive growth in functional energy drinks. Snacks and personal care, at 35% of sales, delivered 4.2% organic, with price/mix driving the gains amid private label pressures from discounters, offset by relaunching air-fried chips that boosted velocity significantly. Household and health rounded out at 4.5% organic, led by volume in disinfectants riding post-pandemic hygiene demand.  

Regionally, North America, 55% of sales, led with 6.5% organic growth, beating peers through e-commerce acceleration to 15% of sales via Amazon exclusives and DTC, plus ACV gains at major retailers. EMEA grew 2.5%, managing inflation headwinds with pricing and sustainable packaging innovations compliant with EU regulations. LATAM and APAC, 25% combined, surged 9.0%, with double-digit gains in Brazil and India from sachet packs and premium skincare amid urbanization.  

Our edge stems from portfolio reshaping, pruning low-margin SKUs to fund dozens of launches with R&D up to $450 million; digital tech like AI demand sensing reducing stockouts; and consumer agility tracking trends like health shifts from GLP-1 medications. Looking ahead, we see mid-single-digit organic growth for the full year, with Q4 at 5-7%.  

Building on that, let's decompose the organic sales growth in more detail. Organic growth came in at 6.1% for Q3, accelerating from prior quarters and outpacing the broader CPG sector's 3-4% average per NielsenIQ, ahead of peers amid softer volumes globally. This balanced mix included +2.3% from volume, +2.4% from price, and +1.4% from favorable mix.  

Volume at +2.3% improved sequentially, reflecting demand recovery as inflation eases. In snacks and nutrition, 35% of sales, volume rose 4.2%, driven by strong penetration of plant-based protein bars capturing share in the $25 billion better-for-you snacks category against Kellogg and Mondelez. Beverages, 25% of sales, saw +3.1% from hydration drinks expanding in e-commerce and convenience stores, functional beverages up 15% versus Red Bull and Monster. Household and personal care, another 25%, grew 0.8% overall, flat in laundry but up 5% in premium eco cleaners aligning with 7% sustainable HPC growth per Nielsen. Beauty and wellness, 15%, dipped -0.5% in mass haircare but held steady in premium serums via DTC.  

Regionally for volume, North America at 50% of sales grew 3.5%, with 2.1 market share points gained per IRI, ACV expanding in snacks. Europe added 1.2%, resilient via discounter wins despite packaging regs. Emerging markets rose 1.8%, Latin America leading at +4% through informal channels, Asia flat post-lockdowns. Our Velocity 2.0 initiative using AI assortment optimization boosted shelf facings 15% and sales per ACV point 9%.  

Pricing contributed +2.4%, down slightly as input inflation cooled to 2-3%, with list increases of 4-6% and 85% pass-through efficiency above industry 70% per BCG. Snacks +3.1% recovering cocoa and nuts; beverages +2.8% on aluminum; household +1.9% with optimized trade spend; beauty +2.0%. North America +3.0% with elasticity -1.8 better than peers; Europe +1.5% under price controls; emerging +2.8% hedged. Our ML pricing models on historical data enabled margin protection.  

Mix added +1.4% from premium and innovation SKUs now 42% of portfolio, up from 35%. Premium/functional +0.9% with plant-based variants driving 300bps margin accretion; channel mix +0.3% as e-comm/DTC hits 18%; geography +0.2% from emerging premium. Portfolio Power culled 12% low-margin SKUs, reinvesting in launches like microbiome cleaners and elite hydration.  

This drove 180bps operating margin expansion. For Q4, expect 5-7% organic with volume +2.5-3.5%, price +1.5-2.0%, mix +1.5%, mitigated by nearshored supply and FX hedges.  

Turning to gross margin, we achieved 42.5%, up 230bps year-over-year and 150bps sequentially, on track for 200bps full-year expansion to 42%. Tailwinds of 550bps included +300bps from pricing across 70% of portfolio, 5-7% on core like energy drinks with 6% hikes supported by loyalty and 8% category growth per Nielsen, and premium snacks shifting to bold flavors via AI pricing on IRI data. Productivity added +200bps via $180 million COGS savings from Vitality Efficiency Network across 25 plants—robotic palletizing cutting labor 15%, 10% yield on snacks, SKU pruning 12% freeing capacity for innovators, regenerative sourcing fixing 40% palm oil amid El Niño spikes.  

Headwinds of 320bps: input inflation -150bps from cocoa +45%, dairy +12%, oils +18%, hedged 75%; freight -100bps from Red Sea reroutes and fuel +8%, offset by nearshoring 15% LatAm production; FX -50bps in EMEA. Regionally, North America 45.2% up 280bps on pricing and automation; EMEA 39.8% up 180bps local sourcing; LatAm 41.5% +250bps hedged; APAC 38.2% +100bps premium traction.  

Our Margin First approach prioritizes structural gains, with blockchain for cocoa, $500M capex in digital twins to lift inventory turns to 10x. Positioned competitively versus Mondelez's compression or P&G's premiums.  

Next, I'll turn the call over to Lisa Patel to discuss marketing and brand performance.  

Lisa Patel:  
Thank you, Michael. We saw strong performance in our core brands, particularly in snacks and beverages. Our digital marketing efforts are driving significant engagement, and we are seeing strong results from our targeted campaigns.  

Let me dive deeper into new product launches and our innovation pipeline, a key growth engine in the CPG space where category growth is low-single digits globally per Nielsen. New products, launched within the last 24 months, accounted for 18% of total net sales, up from 14% a year ago, generating $285 million in incremental revenue at 22% YoY growth, exceeding our 15-20% target. This ties to our $450 million annual R&D at 3.2% of sales, matching leaders like PepsiCo and Unilever.  

Recent launches gained traction across snacks, beverages, and personal care. In snacks, VitalCrisp plant-based high-protein veggie crisps, launched six months ago in North America on clean-label trends—68% consumers seek natural per IRI 2023—hit 12% ACV, 45% repeat rates, 2.5 units/store/week 30% above category, 3.2 share points in $4.2B segment over Mondelēz's Simply Snackin', $120M Q3 sales, margins +250bps to 32% via Midwest sourcing.  

Beverages: HydraBoost RTD functional water with electrolytes, adaptogens like ashwagandha, zero sugar, rolled out EMEA/APAC on 12% CAGR premium hydration per Euromonitor, 8% ACV in UK/Germany with Tesco/Rewe, 2.1% household penetration, 28% YoY dollars, $65M Q3, 28% margins via micro-encapsulation extending shelf life 20%.  

Personal care: EcoGlow sustainable skincare, 98% natural biodegradable in 100% PCR packaging, launched LATAM amid 55% sustainability drivers and Brazil regs, 15% ACV Mexico/Brazil Walmart/Pão de Açúcar, $45M Q3 up 35% seq, e-comm +40% Mercado Libre.  

Pipeline: 25 SKUs next 12 months for $600M Year 1 revenue—40% functional nutrition, 30% health-indulgence, 30% eco-household. Highlight: AI NutriForge with IBM Watson simulating 10,000 iterations/week, cutting dev time 18 to 9 months; BlissBar protein snack Q1 2025 NA, 15g plant protein chocolate, 35% higher preference vs incumbents in $10B bar category chasing Clif.  

North America 60% pipeline on 4% growth, premiumization +15% AUP per Kantar via SnaxElite keto snacks to 20% ACV. EMEA value functionals like HydraBoost vitamin D for Nordics +25% in flat segment. APAC 11% YoY, EcoGlow Indonesia $2B skincare palm-free. LATAM PureShield probiotic cleaners 18% CAGR green cleaning Statista.  

Pillars: consumer-led agility via 50k VOC panels, 70% launches shaped, social listening on gut health +40%; sustainability all meet 2030 PCR, 80% already as 62% Gen Z boycotts non-eco per Deloitte; tech scale $100M agile lines Vietnam +25% capacity -5% COGS. Gaining share vs P&G personal care +1.2 to 14%, Nestlé snacks +0.8 to 11%, 20% faster cycles. Mitigating cocoa/palm volatility hedging/alternatives, clean claims certified. Positions for 8-10% organic FY25 above 3% average.  

On promotional strategy and effectiveness, our cornerstone amid trade spend 20-25% of gross like P&G/Unilever peers. Q3 investment $1.2B, flat YoY at 22.4% revenue via zero-based budgeting. ROI 4.2x up 15% from 3.7x, 12% sales lift promoted weeks, 28% NMV growth 5.2%.  

Event-based 55% spend 14.5% lift, e.g. CrispWave chips +18% volume TPRs. Accrual 30% 3.8x ROI, digital coupons +25% to 45M. AI promo engine with NielsenIQ/Revionics 92% elasticity accuracy store-SKU, cut underperformers 18%, reallocated $150M event stacking; beverages ThirstQuench grill-outs geo-fenced +22% ACV Southeast.  

North America 55% spend 4.5x ROI Amazon Subscribe & Save +32% repeats, e-comm 28% vs Unilever 24%. Europe 4.1x health halo bundles vs Mondelez UK +11% share. Emerging 25% 5.1x Brazil/India hyper-local JioMart cashback soaps +19% volume.  

Bifurcated consumers: Promo Precision ML segments occasions -27% waste. Ahead of Kimberly-Clark 3.5x, our baby care 4.8x influencers. Q4/FY24 target 4.5x +10% efficiency, retailer media top 10 chains 15% off-shelf, blockchain loyalty APAC, right-price vs Colgate EDLP defend 62% oral penetration. Underpins 4-6% organic, 15% EPS.  

Thank you. I'll now turn it over to David Ortiz for supply chain updates.  

David Ortiz:  
Thank you, Lisa. We continue to focus on optimizing our supply chain to improve efficiency and reduce costs. We are implementing new technologies and processes to enhance our responsiveness to changing market conditions. We are also actively working to mitigate the impact of supply chain disruptions, including through hedging, nearshoring, and agile manufacturing like our Vietnam facility boosting APAC capacity. Our efforts contributed to gross margin gains and support innovation scaling.  

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.  

Operator:  
Thank you. Instructions for questions: press star one to queue. Our first question comes from Sarah Lee with JPMorgan.  

Sarah Lee:  
Could you provide more insight into the geographic performance, particularly in developed markets?  

Sarah Thompson:  
Thanks, Sarah. We saw a clear divergence, with developed markets delivering 2.8% organic growth, slightly ahead of expectations and in line with P&G and Unilever. North America, 32% of sales, grew 3.1% on 4.2% pricing in laundry and cleaning like UltraClean pods, flat volume/mix but +50bps share in fabric care per Nielsen via promotions, margins 22.5% +80bps from DC consolidation -1.5% COGS. Western Europe 2.1% organic, -1.8% volume beauty headwinds Germany/UK, +4.0% pricing, premium BioGlow +12% e-comm Amazon/Sephora now 15% beauty sales, e-comm overall 28% up from 22% with AR tools +18% conversions.  

Emerging markets roared at 9.4%, 3x developed, ahead of Reckitt. APAC ex-Japan 11.2%, India/Indonesia double-digits, GlowEssence skincare +2.3 share facial per Kantar on middle class, +7.5% volume +3.7% price; China household detergents +8.9% D2C app 15M users +25%. LATAM 10.1%, Brazil F&B +13% volume 1.2M kirana via micro-distrib Nubank, +4.2% price; MENA 6.8%, Nigeria personal care +15% sachets. FX shaved 2.5pts reported, margins 18.2% palm disruptions hedged 70%. Leaning in with 15% innovation budget reallocation, AI forecasting -22% stockouts APAC, recycled PET LatAm, influencers India 3x ROI, M&A scouting. Developed stability, emerging 60% incremental sales for 5-7% FY24 organic.  

Operator:  
Our next question comes from Mark Johnson with Morgan Stanley.  

Mark Johnson:  
How are you managing inventory levels given the current economic uncertainty?  

Michael Chen:  
Good question, Mark. Inventory management remains a priority, with our AI-driven demand sensing and SAP upgrades keeping fill rates at 98% and stockouts down 25%. We've optimized via Velocity 2.0 for 15% more shelf facings, nearshoring 40% NA/ASEAN footprint, and hedging 80% FX/commodities. Days inventory improved to 8.5x turns, balancing uncertainty without excess, supporting volume recovery and Q4 holiday build.  

Operator:  
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Barclays.  

Emily Chen:  
Can you discuss the progress on your sustainability goals and any related cost implications?  

David Ortiz:  
Absolutely, Emily. Sustainability is embedded, with all new products meeting 2030 PCR packaging goals—80% already achieved—and regenerative sourcing like RSPO palm oil, fixed pricing shielding volatility. EcoGlow 100% PCR biodegradable, PureShield green cleaners. Costs: initial investments in agile lines and certs offset by 5% COGS reductions via automation/yields, +200bps gross margin tailwind. Pilots like blockchain traceability de-risk, aligning with regs like Brazil plastics, no material drag—actually accretive long-term as 62% Gen Z demands it per Deloitte. On track for goals, enhancing brand equity.  

Operator:  
Our next question comes from David Kim with Citi.  

David Kim:  
What are your expectations for pricing elasticity in the coming quarters?  

Lisa Patel:  
Thanks, David. Elasticity remains manageable at -1.8 in NA better than peers' -2.5, thanks to our AI engine forecasting 92% accuracy, dynamic models on IRI/Nielsen data. Q4 we'll test right-price vs EDLP, targeting 85% pass-through on 4-6% lists as inflation eases, balancing with high-ROI promos 4.5x. Premium loyalty in functionals limits downside, expect price +1.5-2.0% contrib to organic without volume sacrifice, defending share.  

Operator:  
There are no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back to Sarah Thompson for closing remarks.  

Sarah Thompson:  
Thank you, Operator, and thank you all for your insightful questions. We remain committed to delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.  

Alex Rivera:  
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the GCB Q3 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
